title: Consumption patterns and threshold playbook
body:
Purpose: quick, reusable worksheet to run a QBR section that reviews token consumption patterns, models of budget exhaustion, rate-limit exposure and templated alert copy for customers. Intended for CSMs to run live during QBRs or to prep as an appendix in renewal decks.

How to use: copy table rows into your QBR slide, update the numbers from Billing UI (last 90/30/7 day windows) and run the sensitivity scenarios (columns below). Highlight the scenario that matches current runway and propose 1–3 mitigating actions.

Sections included:
1) Snapshot metrics (last 30d / 90d) with quick checks
2) Consumption buckets by workload (interactive: chat, embeddings, batch-generation, retriever/rerank)
3) Rate limit exposure ladder (percent of requests that hit rate cap at peak hour)
4) Budget exhaustion sensitivity matrix (3-tier simulations: conservative/moderate/aggressive)
5) Escalation & alert templates (email + in-product banner copy + recommended SLA response time)
6) Recommended mitigation options (short, medium, long term) and cost delta estimates

Notes on data pulls: pull usage CSV from Billing > Usage > export tokens by model and route for the windows; join to product route to split by workload. Use hour-of-day distribution to identify peak-hour rate-cap risk.

Common pitfalls: not aligning embedding-heavy workloads to per-embedding unit metrics; forgetting KV cache hit estimates (can reduce token count by ~25% for retrieval-heavy flows); assuming uniform per-token cost across models — supply model variant in the table.

Quick prep checklist for CSM before QBR:
- Last 90d avg daily tokens and 30d rolling peak hour rate
- Current committed spend vs actual MRR (if on Dedicated)
- Any recent config changes (batching, quantization, model swap)
- Open tickets related to throttling or billing queries

Use-case scenarios to call out in QBR:
- Sudden embedding burst from search reindex (action: temporary rate cap increase + ingest throttling)
- Growth in chat session lengths due to product change (action: tune message truncation + prefix caching)
- Automated agents causing token storms at heart of night timezone (action: schedule dedup / pacing rules)

Worksheet authoring guidance: keep rows concise, add a color-coded column in slide (green/yellow/red) for runway; include recommended SLA commit if customer asks for capacity guarantees (example: +30% peak buffer for 90-day growth >25%).
quick_metrics_table: Avg daily tokens,30d,1,250,000,derived from Billing > CSV (exclude dev/test keys)
Peak hour tokens,30d,180,000,hour with highest aggregate token count (UTC 02:00 - 03:00)
Top 3 routes by tokens,30d,chat-api (62%),embed-api (22%),batch-gen (10%),helps prioritize optimizations
Committed vs actual spend,30d,$12,000 vs $14,900,overspend driven by embedding bursts
sensitivity_matrix_rows: Conservative,+5% monthly growth,1,312,500,No significant overage expected,recommended monitor
Moderate,+20% monthly growth,1,500,000,$1,600 projected overage at current pricing,consider quota adjustment
Aggressive,+50% monthly growth,1,875,000,$8,900 projected overage,recommend immediate engagement for dedicated capacity
rate_limit_ladder: 99th,8,700 RPM,18%,sustained peak hitting rate caps,likely user impact
alert_templates: Email subject: Action required — token consumption accelerating for <PRODUCT-NAME>

Email body: Hi <Customer-Contact>, we saw a sustained increase in token consumption over the last 24–72 hours (peak hour up by <X>%). At the current pace, projected monthly spend will exceed your target by <Y> unless mitigations are applied. Suggested immediate actions: 1) enable rate cap buffer on ingest routes; 2) enable prefix caching for high-frequency prompts; 3) schedule short-term quota increase while we investigate. Reply to escalate and we can provision a temporary buffer within 2 business hours.

In-product banner: We noticed high usage on your account. Tokens this hour are >90% of your configured rate limit. Actions: pause non-critical jobs, review quota settings in Billing > Usage, or contact your CSM.
Pager/Slack short: ALERT — <CLIENT> tokens > 90% peak cap. CSM/Oncall: start throttling policy review, contact eng if sustained >95% for 30m.
Alert severity guidance: P1 — sustained >95% for >30m and customer-facing failures; P2 — repeated >90% spikes causing degraded performance; P3 — one-off spikes under 30m
recommended_actions: Short term (0–72h): enable temporary quota increase (CSM + Ops), add in-product banner, pause non-essential batch jobs
Medium term (3–30d): tune batching window for heavy gen routes, evaluate prefix/KV caching opportunities, shift embedding workloads to smaller model variant for cold-indexing
Long term (30+d): discuss Dedicated/reserved capacity for predictable peaks, implement automated pacing layer in customer app, run a cost-quality evaluation for quantized model variants
example_playbook_steps: 1) In QBR, present Snapshot and call out single color-coded row (runway < 30 days = red)
2) Walk sensitivity matrix and pick scenario matching customer's growth plan
3) Propose immediate action (from recommended actions) with estimated cost delta
4) Open a ticket to Engineering if throttle patterns indicate infra risk and CC product
5) Schedule a follow-up deep-dive (30–60m) with the customer's engineering contact within 5 business days
notes_for_CSM: When asking for numbers from Billing, explicitly request 'tokens by model, by route, hour granularity, last 90 days' to avoid undercounting bursty agents.
If customer is on Dedicated, translate tokens to GPU-hour equivalents using the internal cost sheet (ask FinOps for current GPUEq).
For renewal negotiations, convert projected overage into per-seat or per-feature delta to make uplift tangible (e.g., 10% uplift = $X/mo).
